reading_editions.result: A complete labelled minimum table at level four or higher determines the positive-definite lattice up to a unique marked isometry.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked what a marked distance table actually retains about a lattice. His fixed-observation test leads here to a positive reconstruction result.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The proof starts with a positive-definite lattice and the table of minima. Convexity of its Voronoi cell, polarization and integer generation give the result. The Alpöge–Claude release supplies the application to its labelled theta weights.

reading_editions.result: Two actions on the same polarized fourfold agree on full level $3^{28}$. A point one power deeper separates them.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s question about the information lost in a change of frame led us to hold the lattice metric and the entire torsion observation fixed.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The discriminant bound and the fourfold example use integral operators, quaternions and torus uniformization. The release supplies the level-size requirements and the generic arithmetic-action comparison against which the example is tested.

reading_editions.result: Compare cuts, the shortest roots of $E_8$, and arbitrary unit vectors. The weighted optima distinguish the three constraints.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s earlier golden-rotation and frame questions motivate keeping the allowed directions explicit as one weight changes. His later pointer to Bubeck’s post prompted this particular comparison.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The weighted-cut relaxation is due to Goemans and Williamson. OpenAI supplied the separate matrix-exponent claim. Our calculation compares their formula with a shortest-root constraint and proves a golden-ratio nonattainment result. The Alpöge–Claude input is the particular E₈ matrix and its use in their reference orbit.
reading_editions.first_publication: In the same revision as this collection.

reading_editions.result: The golden limit has an exactly repeating normalized height. At a rational rank-one boundary the cluster set is a full interval.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s GOLD records a rotation and its residual, and Compactification Costs asks which distinctions survive at a boundary. Here the question is what remains after the height is rescaled.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The specific Voronoi seed and fan hypotheses come from the release. The Fibonacci scaling, cluster-set calculation and normal-local-ring argument are the derivations given here.

reading_editions.result: An integral identity inserts any prescribed finite list into a strict support. A binary example gives all twelve entries.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether the same arithmetic objects can survive the change of frame and still meet the required equality.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release defines the support and its equality condition. Lagrange’s identity inserts vectors into any such support. The explicit binary fan and twelve-entry example are worked out here.

reading_editions.result: Matching local elementary divisors allows global maximum slopes separated by an arbitrarily large amount.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s same-observation question asks which global quantities can vary when all the stated local readings agree.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the row predicates, levels and intended bound. The two row lattices and their slope comparison are the project’s construction.

reading_editions.result: Taking a Hermitian quotient before or after a field embedding can give arbitrarily different mean logarithms.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether a metric reading can be transported to a new arithmetic frame without losing the quantity being measured.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: A Hermitian quotient and a change of embedding suffice for the mathematical example. The release supplies the particular quotient bound whose direction is then checked.

reading_editions.result: A self-dual lattice can represent one at every completion and have no global vector of norm one.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s BLA comparison keeps the same curve ideal in view under local valuation and global norm readings. The corpus guide records this application.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the host fields and its ideal-scaling prescription. The norm-one obstruction and local-global comparison are proved for those data.

reading_editions.result: In the binary test, degree $d$ buys at most $\lfloor d/q\rfloor$ extra uniformizer powers on every competing edge.
reading_editions.subject: Lattice geometry and arithmetic actions
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s audit asks how much precision a fixed observation can spend to distinguish competing inputs.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies its source lattice, local rank predicate and Frobenius coordinates. The binary degree bound and its equality examples are independently counted here.

reading_editions.result: An exact theta zero lies on a determinant-one orbit. Its weight and the sharp shortest-lift bound isolate the surviving reference term.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s golden-lattice branch asked where a lost residue can return on the very orbit that carries the claimed estimate.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The E₈ matrix, distinguished slot and congruence predicates are upstream inputs. The shortest-lift theorem, tuned theta zero and reference-weight comparison are proved here. Later size checks are linked above.

reading_editions.result: One theta section vanishes on an entire smaller probe group and recovers the full leading size on the next group. Includes corrected size parameters.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s request to track the missing residue motivates changing only the torsion observation on the very same theta section.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The allowed projection, phases and three size inequalities come from the release. The two-parameter family, Fourier calculation, ideal and Newton check are derived here.

reading_editions.result: An elliptic good factor makes every toric probe of the distinguished section vanish. A different section or torsion label recovers a unit.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s request to probe what a geometric measurement can miss led to holding the good elliptic coordinate fixed as toric precision grows.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the eighth-power polarization and the distinction between a torsion probe and a section index. The elliptic example, root-line calculation and counting bounds are developed here using the cited classical facts.

reading_editions.result: A nonsplit polarization kernel has two order-nine generators where the phase-free kernel has exponent three. Both have 81 elements.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked for the residue carried through a lattice handoff. His phase and fibre questions led to testing the two power maps on one and the same torsion fibre.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The nonsplit example, finite group law and integral obstruction are derived from the elliptic Weil pairing and classical period theory. The release supplies the particular E₈ coordinate factor and inverse matrix tested at the end.
reading_editions.first_publication: In the same revision as this collection.

reading_editions.result: In a nonsplit degeneration each good torsion point misses some uniquely minimized class. A bounded family of probes detects all translated sections.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s fibre question led us to vary the good torsion point while tracing the same Fourier coefficient and the order of the choices.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the primitive-family and individual-probe quantifiers. The moving-zero construction, finite set of detecting probes and comparison use the nonsplit example and the cited classical theta theory.
reading_editions.first_publication: In the same revision as this collection.

reading_editions.result: The same coarse sum can conceal two changed leading digits on genuine Fourier projections.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether the golden-ratio substitution can erase a residue on a genuine lattice input. GOLD and Compactification Costs supply the recorded route to that question.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the particular numerical recipe, its matrix and its geometric caller. The explicit theta periods and the two leading digits are calculated here.

reading_editions.result: A reflection pairs the two true fine sums. The first unpaired point sets the exact precision to which halving the coarse sum recovers them.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang specifically asked about the residue left by a cancellation. The calculation tracks the first lattice point that the pairing can no longer hide.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The example uses the release’s E₈ matrix and numerical reconstruction. The reflection, determinant and exact precision at the first unpaired term are proved here.

reading_editions.result: The residue table has rank 28. Seven more independent directions appear in the next binary digit.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s question about a residue on the residue motivated comparing two successive digits of the same genuine table.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies its lattice and the ordinary-section comparison. The rank calculations and determinant certificate concern the new geometric table constructed in this audit.

reading_editions.result: Coherent class sums can have a limit outside the algebraic closure. At a fixed geometric trait the Galois symmetry constrains the field of values.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s finite-observation and completion questions motivate testing what compatible finite readings can force about one infinite object.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The algebraic-closure counterexample is constructed directly. The positive field-of-values result uses the finite Galois and attained-weight hypotheses stated in the release.

reading_editions.result: Conjugating the coefficients of a nonzero entire function can give a series of radius zero, even after any prescribed finite initial segment.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s Riemann–Pang Ledger supplied the finite-prefix and uncontrolled-tail question. APCI and Abstract Loops ask which further reading can distinguish the two continuations.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The counterexample uses a quadratic field unit and the root test. The release supplies its summation convention and the particular geometric theta subclass whose protection is examined separately.

reading_editions.result: For a totally ramified cyclic extension of prime degree, the ramification break gives the exact loss in approximating an almost invariant element downstairs.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s question about trusting a preserved readout motivates testing how much Galois invariance can be recovered from a congruence.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The cyclic prime-degree digit formula is proved from a uniformizer basis. The release supplies the separate frame-root and invariant-germ construction used in its application.

reading_editions.result: A tail estimate is sharp on a fixed trait. A regular arithmetic surface gives exact precision thresholds for divisor descent.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s work on thresholds and the tails they control motivates keeping the test point and the requested precision in their stated order.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the divisibility and approximation predicates. The lattice estimate, ramified family and sharp cutoffs on an arithmetic surface are calculated directly.

reading_editions.result: A singular arithmetic surface has a computable cutoff. One ramified arc rejects every proposed base generator in a two-blowup example.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s question about what a frame can actually certify motivates testing the same divisibility claim at singular and exceptional points.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the normality and proper-fibre hypotheses and its downstream use. The node, blowup and separating-probe arguments appear here with their commutative-algebra inputs.

reading_editions.result: For infinitely many orders the one-variable jet loses a whole unit of divisibility. The loss is sharp on this specialization.
reading_editions.subject: Theta series, torsion and descent
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s declared-interface test motivates measuring exactly how many digits of a jet survive an integral change of frame.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release provides the jet estimate and its formal hypotheses. The one-variable examples and sharp loss are calculated in this audit.

reading_editions.result: A single Taylor coefficient checks the strict local condition, while a different prime supplies a global witness of order 577.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s local-versus-global reading question is applied to one fixed class. CLEF keeps the two levels of observation explicit in this arithmetic branch.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The field, twist and target strict condition are chosen from the release. The Taylor coefficient and independent global prime are arithmetic witnesses worked out here.

reading_editions.result: An explicit dyadic ideal has order 577 and contributes a class to the arithmetic count.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s corpus asks to keep the same ideal in view when changing from a geometric measurement to an arithmetic one.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the shape of the host, geometric class and arithmetic count. The explicit ideal, its generator and its exact order are calculated for this input.

reading_editions.result: The pure-character part of the 577 count is determined on every sufficiently deep real dyadic layer.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked us to reconstruct the arithmetic rows of rhOfAll and keep one character fixed while the window changes.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the host, twists and normalized plus-count. This paper computes its pure-character contribution and states which other characters remain outside that computation.

reading_editions.result: Each finite layer has a detecting prime even though every fixed finite place eventually loses its detection.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked what changes if a finite list of observations is fixed before moving up the tower. This application is recorded in the corpus guide.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The example uses the cyclotomic host and class singled out in the audit. The two orders of quantification are distinguished with explicit primes and splitting calculations.

reading_editions.result: Two distinct obstructions rule out order 125 for the strict groups on the inputs 2179 and 106619.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s CLEF comparison follows a fixed global class through local measurements at successive coefficient orders.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release sets the strict group being tested. A published conjectural table prompted one input. The divisor and local unit arguments here give the two cutoffs.

reading_editions.result: The unique classical weight-three form in the rank-two alternative has the wrong coefficient modulo five.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s BLA comparison follows the observed contribution into the exact rank-two alternative. The corpus guide explicitly records this use.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release states the alternative and its local conditions. Twisting and the checked Fourier coefficient rule out the proposed rank-two point on this input.

reading_editions.result: Two twists have the same complete residual trace on the stated subgroup and strict groups of orders 577 and one.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s APCI comparison asks whether an entire trace determines the marked arithmetic answer. The corpus guide records the test on these two twists.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the two twists, the host subgroup and the ordered conditions. The matching characteristic polynomials and the separate strict-group computations are the comparison given here.

reading_editions.result: The geometric multiplier erases a nonzero squareclass reading. The proof counts the inputs sharing its image.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s APCI observation-fibre test motivated comparing distinct squareclasses under the same weighted norm. This example is recorded in the corpus guide.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The coefficient minus eighty and the map being measured are taken from the release. The distinct inputs, collision count and downstream check were calculated in the audit.

reading_editions.result: On a CM example integral character sums conceal a denominator present in each of 891 individual class readings.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether observing every transformed sum can certify the original arithmetic entries.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the CM period normalization and the character transform. The class-field example and its 891 individual denominator readings are proved with the cited arithmetic inputs.

reading_editions.result: Direct counts give both sides of the transfer for the stated equal-depth and isolated-singleton families.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s fixed-observation test motivates holding the reported trace data fixed while checking the lattices behind both sides of the transfer.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release defines the two orbital counts. This paper derives their equality for the stated families by lattice counting and checks the finite cases independently.

reading_editions.result: One prime-sum measurement drops a zeta zero. The other three characters recover the missing contribution.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked to take rhOfAll apart and see what each arithmetic row loses before putting the pieces back together.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The four characters and the deduction being dismantled are release inputs. The Euler-product and character reconstruction explains the missing zero for that specified row.

reading_editions.result: At an explicit scale two arithmetic contributions exceed one shared budget. The published eventual threshold lies later.
reading_editions.subject: Arithmetic witnesses and counts
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked to keep the actual scale fixed while combining arithmetic contributions that fit separately.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the window budget and its eventual quantifiers. The two-prime example is a pointwise failure at the stated scale.

reading_editions.result: The supplied mixed intersection returns two in one order and eight in the other. The genuine surface value is four either way.
reading_editions.subject: Geometric models and heights
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang set the declared-interface test. Jenny Lorraine Nielsen’s critique identified the permissive geometry predicate that prompted this particular calculation.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The geometry constructor and its call sites are taken from Alpöge–Claude. Evaluating it in both orders is the project’s counterexample to the mixed classical interpretation.

reading_editions.result: The selected geometry builder fails the release’s stronger asymptotic Riemann–Roch condition. The tested numerical uses carry separate premises.
reading_editions.subject: Geometric models and heights
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether the chosen geometric object earns the separate growth assertion. The project key also credits Nielsen for identifying the permissive predicate.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: This is expressly a countertheorem about the release’s divXFl constructor and its stronger Riemann–Roch condition. The project supplies the counterargument and traces the actual uses.

reading_editions.result: For the specified trivial-character windows the auxiliary coefficient-field degree eventually exceeds every fixed power of the scale.
reading_editions.subject: Geometric models and heights
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s uniformity question asks which parameters can grow while a window estimate is being used.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The release supplies the trivial-character window, host and auxiliary-field construction. The field-degree lower bound is derived on that specific family.

reading_editions.result: A fixed line and metric give different normalized small-section counts when the coefficient fields move with the tensor power.
reading_editions.subject: Geometric models and heights
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang’s scope and uniformity questions motivate keeping the archimedean metric fixed while varying the coefficient field and tensor power.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The project’s moving-field example is computed on a fixed projective line. The paper compares it to the particular small-section estimate in the release.
